html:
In the app

A level project opens with guided mode on this chapter: the panel lists the tags the program needs (Make them), shows every rung below under its fold, checks that MainRoutine verifies, and ticks these results while you run the level:

  • Run mode, Start: the level completes (hopper empty, belt clear)
  • Every bottle in the right bin, none lost
  • Under par (220 s)

Hard · par 220 s

The job

A gravity filler fills each bottle by time: the valve is open for Fill_Time, and what goes in is the flow times the time. The flow does not hold still. The product warms through the run and flows faster; then a fresh, cold tank comes on and it flows slower; and every fill scatters a little. A checkweigher after the filler weighs each bottle on the move and gives the program its net weight in grams (CW_Net), a strobe as each new weight comes in (CW_New) and its verdict (CW_Under, CW_OK, CW_Over). The target is 960 g; the band is 950 to 985 g. Push off every bottle out of the band. Then close the loop: average the last few weights and trim Fill_Time so the average comes back to the target, a little at a time, inside the trim's limits (1460 to 1780 ms, about ±10 % of the nominal 1620 ms); at a limit, light Lamp_Fault. The HMI shows the checkweigher, the weights against the band and your fill time on its trend. +100 per bottle in the band in the good bin, +40 per bottle out of the band caught in the reject bin (product made and thrown away), −100 for one out of the band shipped, −50 for one in the band rejected.

The program

The fill is by time: a TON whose preset is Fill_Time. Each new weight (CW_New) goes into a three-deep FIFO, and when the FIFO is full AVE averages it. Outside a ±2 g dead band round the 960 g target, the fill time is scaled by target over average, clamped to the trim’s limits (1460 to 1780 ms), and the averaging starts again on fresh weights, so one correction is judged before the next is made; at a limit Lamp_Fault lights. A bottle out of the band is marked for the pusher. The scoring rewards the trim: a bottle caught out of band is worth less than one filled right.

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

The rungs

Watch for

Trim on every weight and the loop chases the scatter. The dead band and the fresh average after each correction are what keep it steady.

Run it

Load the program, go to Run mode and leave the level to finish (press Start on its console where it has one). The score card shows how it went, and the guided checks above tick as each result happens. A run of this program on v2.02 completed in about 201 s against a par of 220 s, with 3020 points and nothing wrong.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in. Stop_PB is a plain button here; E_Stop is 1 while healthy

pred.q: Start_PB is off, Run is on, Stop_PB is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  4. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: The run lamp, the checkweigher belt and the out belt follow Run: a checkweigher weighs on the move, it never stops
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false), turns Scale_Run (Checkweigher belt motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false) and turns Out_Run (Out belt motor (checkweigher to the good bin)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Scale_Run) Output Energize does: turns Scale_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. OTE(Out_Run) Output Energize does: turns Out_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: START-UP VALUES, once: the nominal fill time, 1620 ms (96 units at the valve's 60 units/s is 1600 ms; the valve follows T_Fill.TT, which is on for one 20 ms scan less than the preset), the target, and the trim's limits, ±10 % of nominal. After this the trim owns Fill_Time

pred.q: Init_Done is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fill_Time is not written (it keeps its value), Target_Net is not written (it keeps its value), Fill_Min is not written (it keeps its value), Fill_Max is not written (it keeps its value), Hopper_Left is not written (it keeps its value) and Init_Done is left as it was. It stops at XIO(Init_Done).

rungs.words: When Init_Done (The fill time and the limits have been set) is off, the rung puts 1620 into Fill_Time (The fill time, ms: what the valve is open for. Shown on the console display and on the HMI's trend), puts 960 into Target_Net (Target net weight, g), puts 1460 into Fill_Min (Trim limit: the shortest fill time, ms), puts 1780 into Fill_Max (Trim limit: the longest fill time, ms), puts 30 into Hopper_Left (Shown on the toolbar) and latches Init_Done on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Init_Done) Examine If Open asks: true when Init_Done is off.
  2. A branch of 6 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(1620,Fill_Time) Move does: puts 1620 into Fill_Time. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(960,Target_Net) Move does: puts 960 into Target_Net. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(1460,Fill_Min) Move does: puts 1460 into Fill_Min. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 4
    1. MOV(1780,Fill_Max) Move does: puts 1780 into Fill_Max. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 5
    1. MOV(30,Hopper_Left) Move does: puts 30 into Hopper_Left. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 6
    1. OTL(Init_Done) Output Latch does: latches Init_Done on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Init_Done stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: RELEASE one bottle when there is none between the hopper and the filler: In_Flight latches in the same scan, so Infeed_Release is on for one scan, one rising edge. The next bottle comes when this one has been filled and moved on, so it reaches the filler after this one has been weighed
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Infeed_Ready (Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released) is on and In_Flight (A bottle is between the hopper and the filler, or under it) is off, each path is tested on its own: it latches In_Flight on; it turns Infeed_Release (Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)) on (and off whenever the rung is false); if this is the first scan of it, it makes Hopper_Left (Shown on the toolbar) = Hopper_Left − 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Infeed_Ready) Examine If Closed asks: true when Infeed_Ready is on.
  3. XIO(In_Flight) Examine If Open asks: true when In_Flight is off.
  4. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTL(In_Flight) Output Latch does: latches In_Flight on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTE(Infeed_Release) Output Energize does: turns Infeed_Release on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
    Path 3
    1. ONS(Rel_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rel_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
    2. SUB(Hopper_Left,1,Hopper_Left) Subtract does: makes Hopper_Left = Hopper_Left − 1. Every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: In_Flight stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: THE MAIN BELT stops when a bottle that has not had its fill reaches PE_Fill (it is standing under the nozzle), and runs again once it has

pred.q: Run is on, PE_Fill is off and Filled is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Conveyor_Run is on.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and either (PE_Fill (Presence eye under the filler nozzle) is off) or (Filled (The bottle under the nozzle has had its fill) is on), the rung turns Conveyor_Run (Main belt motor (hopper to the filler)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIO(PE_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Fill is off.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(Filled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Filled is on.
  3. OTE(Conveyor_Run) Output Energize does: turns Conveyor_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: THE FILL, BY TIME: the timer's preset is Fill_Time, the value the trim adjusts. The valve does not measure anything: what goes in is the flow times the time, and the flow drifts
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, PE_Fill (Presence eye under the filler nozzle) is on and Filled (The bottle under the nozzle has had its fill) is off, the rung runs the timer T_Fill (The fill: the valve is open while it times, preset Fill_Time) toward Fill_Time.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(PE_Fill) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Fill is on.
  3. XIO(Filled) Examine If Open asks: true when Filled is off.
  4. TON(T_Fill,Fill_Time,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Fill toward Fill_Time. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Fill counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: The valve is open while the fill timer times

pred.q: T_Fill.TT is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fill_Valve is off. It stops at XIC(T_Fill.TT).

rungs.words: When T_Fill.TT (the timing bit of T_Fill: The fill: the valve is open while it times, preset Fill_Time) is on, the rung turns Fill_Valve (Filler valve: product runs while it is on (fill by time)) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Fill.TT) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Fill.TT is on.
  2. OTE(Fill_Valve) Output Energize does: turns Fill_Valve on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: Fill done
rungs.words: When T_Fill.DN (the done bit of T_Fill: The fill: the valve is open while it times, preset Fill_Time) is on, the rung latches Filled (The bottle under the nozzle has had its fill) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Fill.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Fill.DN is on.
  2. OTL(Filled) Output Latch does: latches Filled on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Filled stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: The filled bottle has left PE_Fill: ready for the next

pred.q: Filled is on and PE_Fill is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Filled is unlatched and In_Flight is unlatched.

rungs.words: When Filled (The bottle under the nozzle has had its fill) is on and PE_Fill (Presence eye under the filler nozzle) is off, the rung unlatches Filled and unlatches In_Flight (A bottle is between the hopper and the filler, or under it).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Filled) Examine If Closed asks: true when Filled is on.
  2. XIO(PE_Fill) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Fill is off.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(Filled) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Filled. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(In_Flight) Output Unlatch does: unlatches In_Flight. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Filled when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: A NEW WEIGHT: New_Weight strobes once per bottle, so ONS loads each bottle's net weight into the FIFO once
rungs.words: When CW_New (Checkweigher: on for 0.25 s when CW_Net takes a new bottle's weight) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung loads CW_Net (Checkweigher: the net weight of the last bottle across, grams (held until the next)) into the queue Wt_Q[0] (The last three net weights, g (a FIFO; the average is taken when it is full, then it starts again)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(CW_New) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_New is on.
  2. ONS(New_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in New_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. FFL(CW_Net,Wt_Q[0],Wt_Ctl,3,0) FIFO Load does: loads CW_Net into the queue Wt_Q[0]. One entry per false-to-true transition.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
Each part’s data goes in at one end when the part is seen and comes out at the other when the part arrives, in the order the parts came.
pats.think: a ticket roll at a deli counter: the first ticket torn off is the first one served.
pats.watch: A load and an unload must happen once per part each. A part that leaves the line between the two (a reject, a part picked off) has to be unloaded too, or every answer after it belongs to the wrong part.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: THE RUNNING AVERAGE: with three weights in, average them. One bottle scatters (the fill-to-fill spread); three together show where the filler is

pred.q: Wt_Ctl.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: AVE does not run. It stops at XIC(Wt_Ctl.DN).

rungs.words: When Wt_Ctl.DN (the done bit of Wt_Ctl: FIFO control for Wt_Q) is on, the rung averages Wt_Q[0] (The last three net weights, g (a FIFO; the average is taken when it is full, then it starts again)) into Avg_Net (The average of the three, g).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Wt_Ctl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Wt_Ctl.DN is on.
  2. AVE(Wt_Q[0],0,Avg_Net,Ave_Ctl,3,0) Average does: averages Wt_Q[0] into Avg_Net.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: How far the average is from the target, g
rungs.words: When Ave_Ctl.DN (the done bit of Ave_Ctl: Control for the AVE) is on, the rung makes Avg_Err (The average less the target, g) = Avg_Net (The average of the three, g) − Target_Net (Target net weight, g).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Ave_Ctl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Ave_Ctl.DN is on.
  2. SUB(Avg_Net,Target_Net,Avg_Err) Subtract does: makes Avg_Err = Avg_Net − Target_Net. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: THE TRIM: outside a ±2 g dead band, scale the fill time by target over average: 940 g at 1620 ms says 960 g wants 1620 × 960 / 940 = 1654 ms
rungs.words: When Ave_Ctl.DN (the done bit of Ave_Ctl: Control for the AVE) is on and either (Avg_Err (The average less the target, g) is greater than 2) or (Avg_Err is less than -2), the rung computes Fill_Time (The fill time, ms: what the valve is open for. Shown on the console display and on the HMI's trend) = Fill_Time*Target_Net/Avg_Net.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Ave_Ctl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Ave_Ctl.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. GRT(Avg_Err,2) Greater Than asks: true when Avg_Err is greater than 2.
    Path 2
    1. LES(Avg_Err,-2) Less Than asks: true when Avg_Err is less than -2.
  3. CPT(Fill_Time,Fill_Time*Target_Net/Avg_Net) Compute does: computes Fill_Time = Fill_Time*Target_Net/Avg_Net.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.
pats.think: meeting a train. You cannot stand at one exact inch of track and wait for it to stop there; you watch the whole platform.
pats.watch: An EQU on a measured value (a position, a level, a weight) may never be true: the value jumps from just under to just over between scans.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: THE TRIM'S LIMITS: never shorter than 1460 ms nor longer than 1780 ms. A filler that needs more than that is not drifting, it is broken (a blocked nozzle, an empty tank): the trim must not chase it
rungs.words: When Ave_Ctl.DN (the done bit of Ave_Ctl: Control for the AVE) is on, each path is tested on its own: if Fill_Time (The fill time, ms: what the valve is open for. Shown on the console display and on the HMI's trend) is less than Fill_Min (Trim limit: the shortest fill time, ms), it puts Fill_Min into Fill_Time; if Fill_Time is greater than Fill_Max (Trim limit: the longest fill time, ms), it puts Fill_Max into Fill_Time.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Ave_Ctl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Ave_Ctl.DN is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. LES(Fill_Time,Fill_Min) Less Than asks: true when Fill_Time is less than Fill_Min.
    2. MOV(Fill_Min,Fill_Time) Move does: puts Fill_Min into Fill_Time. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. GRT(Fill_Time,Fill_Max) Greater Than asks: true when Fill_Time is greater than Fill_Max.
    2. MOV(Fill_Max,Fill_Time) Move does: puts Fill_Max into Fill_Time. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: START A FRESH AVERAGE: the weights in it were filled at the old time; the next three are filled at the new one

pred.q: Ave_Ctl.DN is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Wt_Ctl is reset.

rungs.words: When Ave_Ctl.DN (the done bit of Ave_Ctl: Control for the AVE) is on, the rung resets Wt_Ctl (FIFO control for Wt_Q).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Ave_Ctl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Ave_Ctl.DN is on.
  2. RES(Wt_Ctl) Reset does: resets Wt_Ctl. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: At a limit: the trim can do no more
rungs.words: When either (Fill_Time (The fill time, ms: what the valve is open for. Shown on the console display and on the HMI's trend) is at most Fill_Min (Trim limit: the shortest fill time, ms)) or (Fill_Time is at least Fill_Max (Trim limit: the longest fill time, ms)), the rung turns Trim_Limit (The fill time is at one of its limits: the filler needs a look) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. LEQ(Fill_Time,Fill_Min) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Fill_Time is at most Fill_Min.
    Path 2
    1. GEQ(Fill_Time,Fill_Max) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Fill_Time is at least Fill_Max.
  2. OTE(Trim_Limit) Output Energize does: turns Trim_Limit on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: A moving value can step over any single number between two scans; a window catches it on the way through.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: The fault lamp tells the operator

pred.q: Trim_Limit is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Fault is off. It stops at XIC(Trim_Limit).

rungs.words: When Trim_Limit (The fill time is at one of its limits: the filler needs a look) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp: the fill time is at a trim limit) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Trim_Limit) Examine If Closed asks: true when Trim_Limit is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: OUT OF BAND: the checkweigher's verdict on the bottle just weighed. It is the next bottle to reach the pusher: one bottle at a time between the checkweigher and the pusher
rungs.words: When CW_New (Checkweigher: on for 0.25 s when CW_Net takes a new bottle's weight) is on, this is the first scan of it and either (CW_Under (Checkweigher: the last bottle was under the band) is on) or (CW_Over (Checkweigher: the last bottle was over the band) is on), the rung latches Reject_Next (The bottle just weighed is out of band) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(CW_New) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_New is on.
  2. ONS(Rej_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Rej_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(CW_Under) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_Under is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(CW_Over) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_Over is on.
  4. OTL(Reject_Next) Output Latch does: latches Reject_Next on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Reject_Next stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: The counts on the toolbar
rungs.words: When CW_New (Checkweigher: on for 0.25 s when CW_Net takes a new bottle's weight) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if CW_Under (Checkweigher: the last bottle was under the band) is on, it makes Under_Count (Shown on the toolbar) = Under_Count + 1; if CW_Over (Checkweigher: the last bottle was over the band) is on, it makes Over_Count (Shown on the toolbar) = Over_Count + 1; if CW_OK (Checkweigher: the last bottle was in the band) is on, it makes Good_Count (Shown on the toolbar) = Good_Count + 1.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(CW_New) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_New is on.
  2. ONS(Cnt_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Cnt_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(CW_Under) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_Under is on.
    2. ADD(Under_Count,1,Under_Count) Add does: makes Under_Count = Under_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(CW_Over) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_Over is on.
    2. ADD(Over_Count,1,Over_Count) Add does: makes Over_Count = Over_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(CW_OK) Examine If Closed asks: true when CW_OK is on.
    2. ADD(Good_Count,1,Good_Count) Add does: makes Good_Count = Good_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: AT THE PUSHER: arm it if the bottle arriving is the one marked
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and this is the first scan of it, each path is tested on its own: if Reject_Next (The bottle just weighed is out of band) is on, it latches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) on; it unlatches Reject_Next.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. ONS(PR_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in PR_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Reject_Next) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reject_Next is on.
    2. OTL(Fire) Output Latch does: latches Fire on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(Reject_Next) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Reject_Next. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: Fire stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.

rungs.head: Rung 20
rungs.comment: Push while the bottle is at the eye

pred.q: PE_Reject is on and Fire is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Reject is on.

rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is on and Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected) is on, the rung turns Reject (Reject pusher cylinder) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(PE_Reject) Examine If Closed asks: true when PE_Reject is on.
  2. XIC(Fire) Examine If Closed asks: true when Fire is on.
  3. OTE(Reject) Output Energize does: turns Reject on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.comment: The bottle has gone: disarm
rungs.words: When PE_Reject (Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher) is off, the rung unlatches Fire (Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(PE_Reject) Examine If Open asks: true when PE_Reject is off.
  2. OTU(Fire) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Fire. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Fire when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

Out_Run.desc: Out belt motor (checkweigher to the good bin)

Init_Done.desc: The fill time and the limits have been set

Fill_Time.desc: The fill time, ms: what the valve is open for. Shown on the console display and on the HMI's trend

Fill_Min.desc: Trim limit: the shortest fill time, ms

Fill_Max.desc: Trim limit: the longest fill time, ms

Infeed_Ready.desc: Hopper exit clear: a bottle can be released

In_Flight.desc: A bottle is between the hopper and the filler, or under it

Infeed_Release.desc: Release one bottle onto the belt (rising edge)

PE_Fill.desc: Presence eye under the filler nozzle

Filled.desc: The bottle under the nozzle has had its fill

Conveyor_Run.desc: Main belt motor (hopper to the filler)

T_Fill.desc: The fill: the valve is open while it times, preset Fill_Time

Fill_Valve.desc: Filler valve: product runs while it is on (fill by time)

CW_New.desc: Checkweigher: on for 0.25 s when CW_Net takes a new bottle's weight

CW_Net.desc: Checkweigher: the net weight of the last bottle across, grams (held until the next)

Wt_Q.desc: The last three net weights, g (a FIFO; the average is taken when it is full, then it starts again)

Avg_Net.desc: The average of the three, g

Avg_Err.desc: The average less the target, g

Trim_Limit.desc: The fill time is at one of its limits: the filler needs a look

Lamp_Fault.desc: Fault lamp: the fill time is at a trim limit

CW_Under.desc: Checkweigher: the last bottle was under the band

CW_Over.desc: Checkweigher: the last bottle was over the band

Reject_Next.desc: The bottle just weighed is out of band

CW_OK.desc: Checkweigher: the last bottle was in the band

PE_Reject.desc: Presence eye ahead of the reject pusher

Fire.desc: Armed: the bottle at the pusher is to be rejected
